memory_update.text: POWL should remain in the node universe as a direct electrical balance-of-plant candidate: medium-voltage switchgear, packaged power systems, record backlog, and disclosed data-center megaproject orders.
MOD should remain in the node universe as a thermal-management candidate: Airedale data-center cooling, liquid/air hybrid systems, controls, and high-density cooling exposure.
WLDN should be tracked as a smaller grid-adjacent engineering hypothesis after the APG acquisition; key verification is whether data-center substation/interconnection work becomes material.

Data-center electrical/thermal balance-of-plant appears constrained not only by major OEMs but also by switchgear capacity, thermal-management assemblies, substation design, interconnection engineering, and field execution.

The highest-potential underfollowed gap is likely among companies classified as industrial electrical equipment, HVAC/thermal, engineering services, or utility consulting rather than AI/cloud infrastructure.

node: Data-center electrical and thermal balance-of-plant: transformers, switchgear, UPS, busway, power distribution, liquid cooling, monitoring, and field services
summary: This pass expands the universe around data-center electrical and thermal balance-of-plant. The clean reference anchor remains Vertiv, but the more Serenity-relevant underfollowed lane points to vendors whose products or services sit one step away from GPUs: medium-voltage switchgear, packaged electrical systems, liquid/precision cooling, electrical infrastructure components, and grid-interconnection engineering. Current evidence is strongest for Powell Industries and Modine because both have explicit data-center/AI-related disclosures. Willdan is a smaller, more speculative grid-adjacent engineering candidate after acquiring APG for data-center substation and interconnection expertise. Vertiv is included only as a reference benchmark, not as an underfollowed discovery candidate.
